note: AUTHORED living-layer boundaries (water and foliage) in MASTER px. These exist because the material mask fails above the river: mask-bare-ground looks for bright low-variance silk and the dry CLIFF up here is bright low-variance silk too — living/native/w-midstream/mask-overlay.png is blue confetti over rock, and 449 mask components with a largest of 6487px is what that looks like numerically. What separates water here is pictorial, so it is authored by eye against gridded master crops (living/grid-crop.py), the same loop the 31 stations used. Two inventory boxes in regions.json were also refuted by looking: f-left-tall-fall [980,8650,1330,10100] is bare cliff and canopy — the real gorge fall is a slender white column at x~1470-1610 running y 9040-10620; and w-upper-stream is not a stream at all, it is the same fall's lower half.  2026-08-20 — THE SUMMITS. The whole band above y~3850 had no living region at all, which is why the highest stations framed a picture that held perfectly still. The three `drift` (mist) regions in regions.json cannot supply it: measured, 40% of each of those boxes reads as 'ink' and that ink is the MOUNTAIN (max stroke thickness 59-75px), with 2.4-2.7% thin stroke — displacing it wobbles the silhouette, which is the smear the inventory feared (living/evidence-mist-has-no-ink.png). There is no mist ink in this painting; the mist IS bare silk. What is really up there and really moves is FOLIAGE, so the summits get gusts like everything else, at half amplitude for distance (class `gust-far`).
